added_models.model: IL-13-humanised OVA-sensitised mouse dosed with tralokinumab

engagement.model: IL-13-humanised OVA-sensitised mouse dosed with tralokinumab
engagement.note: Tralokinumab reduced AHR and BAL eosinophilia after OVA challenge in mice carrying human IL-13; the readouts were AHR and BAL eosinophils.
engagement.short: Tralokinumab cuts humanised-mouse AHR and eosinophils
engagement.quote: In vivo in humanized mouse and cynomolgus monkey antigen challenge models CAT-354 inhibited airways hyperresponsiveness and bronchoalveolar lavage eosinophilia.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; online 2011-09-08 (PubMed), print May 2012. The FDA BLA 761180 integrated review lists the study as CAT354Rp043 (BALB/c male mice).
engagement.judgement: A genetically distinct system from Wills-Karp's wild-type OVA mouse: tralokinumab does not bind mouse IL-13, so the product was dosed only here, and this system states eosinophil reduction where the wild-type system stated eosinophil-independence. Opens at the online date.

engagement.model: IL-13-humanised OVA-sensitised mouse dosed with tralokinumab
engagement.note: MESOS: tralokinumab 300 mg q2w left bronchial, sputum and blood eosinophils unchanged (bronchial ratio 1.43) while FeNO and IgE fell.
engagement.quote: Tralokinumab did not significantly affect eosinophilic inflammation in bronchial submucosa, blood, or sputum compared with placebo, but did reduce FENO and IgE concentrations.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only (n=79, 12 weeks); registry date is the MESOS results posting. AHR, the model's other readout, was never measured as a PD endpoint in a member trial.
engagement.judgement: The product itself, at the phase 3 regimen, did not reproduce the eosinophil reduction its own mouse package predicted; FeNO and IgE moved, so this is a wrong readout prediction rather than a failure of target neutralisation.
engagement.reason: Eosinophil readout did not move in patients
engagement.magnitude_basis: bronchial eosinophil treatment-effect ratio 1.43 (95% CI 0.63-3.27) against inhibition of BAL eosinophilia in the model

efficacy.model: IL-13-humanised OVA-sensitised mouse dosed with tralokinumab
efficacy.note: Tralokinumab inhibited AHR and BAL eosinophilia after OVA challenge in IL-13-humanised mice; the package targeted severe uncontrolled asthma.
efficacy.short: Humanised mouse backs tralokinumab in asthma
efficacy.quote: The preclinical data presented here support the trialling of this mAb in patients with moderate to severe uncontrolled asthma.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; online 2011-09-08, print May 2012. Filed as CAT354Rp043 in the atopic-dermatitis BLA 761180, not in an asthma filing.
efficacy.judgement: Opener on the only mouse the product was dosed in; a separate track from the wild-type OVA mouse (different model, different stated eosinophil prediction).

efficacy.model: IL-13-humanised OVA-sensitised mouse dosed with tralokinumab
efficacy.note: Tralokinumab phase 2a: ACQ-6 primary missed (-0.76 vs -0.61, p=0.375) in 194 moderate-severe asthmatics; FEV1 +0.15 L (p=0.072) not significant.
efficacy.quote: At week 13, change from baseline in ACQ-6 was -0.76±1.04 for tralokinumab versus -0.61±0.90 for placebo (p=0.375).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract only; epub 2012-06-27, print February 2013; registry results posted 2017-02-23. A lung-function signal was present as a secondary (p=0.072).
efficacy.judgement: First member trial of the product the model was dosed with; contra on the primary-endpoint rule, the authors calling the result mixed. Scored here as well as on the wild-type mouse because the two are different systems.

patient_trials.quote: At week 13, change from baseline in ACQ-6 was -0.76±1.04 for tralokinumab versus -0.61±0.90 for placebo (p=0.375).

efficacy.model: IL-13-humanised OVA-sensitised mouse dosed with tralokinumab
efficacy.note: STRATOS 1/2 missed their exacerbation primaries at 300 mg q2w (all-comers rate ratio 0.93; FeNO-high 0.84); TROPOS missed its OCS-sparing primary.
efficacy.short: Phase 3 exacerbation and OCS primaries missed
efficacy.quote: These inconsistent effects on AAER do not support a key role for interleukin 13 in severe asthma exacerbations.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; STRATOS registry results 2018-03-21 (STRATOS 2) and 2018-04-17 (STRATOS 1). TROPOS from Busse 2019 (PMID 30442714, online 2018-11-18, registry results 2018-05-16). Brightling 2015 (phase 2b, NCT01402986) is listed but not scored: its FEV1 secondary was significant.
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens: the product dosed in the model failed both phase 3 exacerbation trials and the OCS-sparing trial, after which AstraZeneca stopped asthma development.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: AAER rate ratio 0.93 (STRATOS 1 all-comers); OCS reduction 37.6% vs 29.9% (TROPOS)

patient_trials.quote: In the STRATOS 1 all-comers population, tralokinumab every 2 weeks did not significantly reduce AAER compared with placebo (7·0% reduction [95% CI -20·8 to 28·4]; rate ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·72 to 1·21]; p=0·59).

In the STRATOS 2 FENO-high population, tralokinumab every 2 weeks (n=108) did not significantly improve AAER (15·8% reduction [95% CI -33·7 to 47·0]; rate ratio 0·84 [95% CI 0·53 to 1·34]; p=0·47) compared with placebo (n=121).
At week 40, the percentage reduction from baseline in the final daily average OCS dose was not significantly different between tralokinumab and placebo (37.62% versus 29.85%; p=0.271).

The annual asthma exacerbation rate at week 52 was similar between patients receiving tralokinumab every 2 weeks (0.91 per patient per year [95% CI 0.76-1.08]) and every 4 weeks (0.97 [0.81-1.14]), and those receiving placebo (0.90 [0.75-1.08]).

added_models.model: Whole-lung allergen challenge in mild allergic asthmatics (late asthmatic response, lebrikizumab)

efficacy.model: Whole-lung allergen challenge in mild allergic asthmatics (late asthmatic response, lebrikizumab)
efficacy.note: Genentech ran lebrikizumab (MILR1444A) 5 mg/kg q4w against the late asthmatic response to inhaled allergen in 29 mild allergic asthmatics (Dec 2008 to Nov 2009).
efficacy.quote: A Phase II, Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Parallel-Group, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of MILR1444A in the Prevention of Allergen-Induced Airway Obstruction in Adults With Mild Allergic Asthma
efficacy.confidence_note: Opening year is the registry start (first posted 2008-10-29, started 2008-12); no results were ever posted. The FDA lebrikizumab review (BLA 761306, atopic dermatitis) does not mention the challenge study.
efficacy.judgement: Opening untested entry at the first dated member use of the human allergen-challenge model; decision 8 puts the challenge in scope as a non-animal system. Patient-level exploratory finding (biomarker-high responders) belongs to the existing periostin track.

efficacy.model: Whole-lung allergen challenge in mild allergic asthmatics (late asthmatic response, lebrikizumab)
efficacy.note: Challenge: LAR cut 48% (95% CI -19 to 90, n.s.), larger in eosinophil/IgE/periostin-high subjects; Noonan: FEV1 primary missed in 212 ICS-free mild-moderate asthmatics.
efficacy.short: Challenge said yes; mild-asthma FEV1 trial missed
efficacy.quote: Blocking IL-13, a single cytokine, in this population of asthmatic patients is insufficient to improve lung function.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both papers. The challenge result (Scheerens 2014, PMID 24131304, online 2013-10-18, print January 2014) became public after Noonan 2013 (epub 2013-05-29), so the comparison dates to 2013. The model's own 48% LAR reduction was not significant (n=29); a re-scorer who reads that as no prediction leaves the track untested. NCT00971035 never posted results.
efficacy.judgement: Paired, not stated. Scheerens' own conclusion is positive ('Lebrikizumab reduced the LAR in subjects with mild asthma') and it sets that beside MILLY's FEV1 gain in ICS-uncontrolled asthma (a same, listed under patient_trials); but the trial nearest the challenge population, ICS-free mild-to-moderate asthma, missed its FEV1 primary, and one contra outranks a same on a track.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: model: LAR FEV1 AUC 2-8 h reduced 48% vs placebo (95% CI -19 to 90); trial: relative FEV1 change neither statistically nor clinically significant vs placebo
efficacy.population: Mild allergic asthmatics (challenge); mild-to-moderate asthma without ICS (trial)

patient_trials.quote: The mean relative change in FEV1 was numerically higher in all lebrikizumab dose groups versus the placebo group, although the difference was neither statistically nor clinically significant.
At week 12, the mean increase in FEV(1) was 5.5 percentage points higher in the lebrikizumab group than in the placebo group (P = 0.02).

efficacy.model: Whole-lung allergen challenge in mild allergic asthmatics (late asthmatic response, lebrikizumab)
efficacy.note: Phase 3 replicate in 310 ICS-free mild-moderate asthmatics: FEV1 +83 mL vs placebo (95% CI -3 to 170, p=0.06), primary missed.
efficacy.quote: Lebrikizumab did not significantly improve FEV1 in mild-to-moderate asthma patients at a dose expected to inhibit the IL-13 pathway.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; epub 2017-12-13, print January 2018; registry results (NCT02104674) posted 2026-07-17, long after the epub that dates the entry.
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens: the second trial in the population closest to the challenge subjects (mild asthma, no ICS) reproduced the miss, and the authors say so.
efficacy.reason: Two FEV1 trials missed in mild asthma
efficacy.magnitude_basis: FEV1 difference 83 mL, p=0.06, against a 48% LAR reduction in the challenge
efficacy.population: Mild allergic asthmatics (challenge); mild-to-moderate asthma without ICS (trial)

patient_trials.quote: Inhibiting IL-13 in this patient population was not sufficient to improve lung function.

added_models.model: Integrated population PK/PD dose-exposure-FEV1 model of tralokinumab (phase 2a/2b data)

dose.model: Integrated population PK/PD dose-exposure-FEV1 model of tralokinumab (phase 2a/2b data)
dose.note: A population PK/PD model pooling phase 2a/2b data predicted near-maximal FEV1 at 300 mg q2w and set the phase 3 regimen.
dose.short: Model picked 300 mg q2w for phase 3
dose.quote: Near-maximal FEV1 increase was predicted at a dose of 300 mg SC once every 2 weeks (Q2W).
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; epub 2017-09-28, print May 2018. The model was built for phase 3 dose selection before the STRATOS results (registry 2018-03-21), so its prediction was prospective. Not found in the tralokinumab FDA review (BLA 761180, atopic dermatitis).
dose.judgement: A separate in-silico system from the cynomolgus track: the only member model that stated a human regimen target. Opens untested at its online date.

dose.model: Integrated population PK/PD dose-exposure-FEV1 model of tralokinumab (phase 2a/2b data)
dose.note: 300 mg q2w, the model's near-maximal FEV1 dose, was given in STRATOS 1/2; both exacerbation primaries missed and asthma development stopped.
dose.quote: In the STRATOS 1 all-comers population, tralokinumab every 2 weeks did not significantly reduce AAER compared with placebo (7·0% reduction [95% CI -20·8 to 28·4]; rate ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·72 to 1·21]; p=0·59).
dose.confidence_note: Abstract only. The model predicted FEV1, not exacerbations; STRATOS FEV1 secondaries are not in the abstract, so the contra is derived from the primary-endpoint failure under the dose table (reached, failed, abandoned).
dose.judgement: Case 'reached, failed, abandoned': the regimen the model chose was tested and the programme ended; counted once, as a derived dose failure, with efficacy carried on the animal tracks.
dose.magnitude_basis: AAER rate ratio 0.93 at the model-selected 300 mg q2w

engagement.model: Mathematical model of blood and airway eosinophil dynamics under anti-IL-13 therapy
engagement.note: A QSP model of eosinophil dynamics predicted lebrikizumab/tralokinumab raise blood eosinophils (30%/10%) while lowering airway eosinophils.
engagement.short: QSP model: blood eosinophils up, airway down
engagement.quote: For the anti-IL-13 therapies, lebrikizumab and tralokinumab, the model predicted an increase of 30% and 10% in total and activated EOS in the blood, respectively, and a decrease in the total and activated EOS in the airways.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; PubMed date 2016-11-26, print November 2016. The model was built after the phase 2 blood-eosinophil observations it reproduces.
engagement.judgement: Opens the in-silico eosinophil track at its first use; the same paper then states the comparison (next entry).

engagement.model: Mathematical model of blood and airway eosinophil dynamics under anti-IL-13 therapy
engagement.note: The paper sets its predicted blood-eosinophil rise beside the published lebrikizumab and tralokinumab phase 2 eosinophil data and calls them consistent.
engagement.quote: All model-based predictions were consistent with published clinical observations.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only; which clinical datasets were used is not visible at abstract level.
engagement.judgement: A retrodiction: built after the clinic had seen blood eosinophils rise on anti-IL-13 antibodies, so retro, never same (decision 10).
engagement.magnitude_basis: blood eosinophil change: model +30% (lebrikizumab), +10% (tralokinumab) against published phase 2 observations (values not in the abstract)

engagement.model: Mathematical model of blood and airway eosinophil dynamics under anti-IL-13 therapy
engagement.note: MESOS: the model's prospective prediction of lower airway eosinophils failed; tralokinumab left bronchial submucosal and sputum eosinophils unchanged.
engagement.quote: Tralokinumab did not significantly affect eosinophilic inflammation in bronchial submucosa, blood, or sputum compared with placebo, but did reduce FENO and IgE concentrations.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only (n=79); subgroup figures (blood ratio 1.21, p=0.055; sputum 0.57, p=0.63) are from the published results as recorded by the checker, not re-read here. The blood half of the prediction is not contradicted; the airway half is.
engagement.judgement: The model's first prospective prediction after the retrodiction (decision 10): airway eosinophils were measured in MESOS and did not fall, so the track turns contra.
engagement.reason: Airway eosinophil prediction failed in MESOS
engagement.magnitude_basis: bronchial eosinophil treatment-effect ratio 1.43 (95% CI 0.63-3.27) and sputum 0.57 (p=0.63) against a predicted decrease

considered_not_added: Zhu 2017 lebrikizumab population PK and exposure-response (PMID 28843617, doi:10.1016/j.pupt.2017.08.010): an analysis of the LAVOLTA phase 3 data itself, published 2017-08 after the trials; it states no prospective dose prediction to compare, and the phase 2-based model that chose 37.5/125 mg q4w was not found published.

Docking model of IL-13 Q144 (rs20541) binding to tralokinumab and lebrikizumab (PMID 29155876, PLoS One 2017): in-silico responder prediction; no member trial stratified by rs20541 found, so no patient comparison.

Human precision-cut lung slices with an antibody 'similar to lebrikizumab' (PMID 30500834, PLoS One 2018): not the product, and the source compares with rodent and primate slices, not with patient results.
IL13 human genetics (R130Q / rs20541 gain-of-function association): no loss-of-function genotype and no member comparison; not a human_genetic model here.
Gauvreau 2011 IMA-638 / IMA-026 allergen challenge (PMID 21057005): the class's human-challenge precedent, but anrukinzumab is not a listed member (checker's own note), so not scorable.

TROPOS (NCT02281357; Busse 2019, PMID 30442714) and Korenblat 2018 (PMID 29413502): patient-side results for the existing cynomolgus, wild-type OVA mouse and hbe-il13-signature tracks; added_models takes only systems without a track, so they appear here only as patient_trials on the humanised-mouse track and as the strengthening entry on the allergen-challenge track.
Dectrekumab / QAX576: no asthma model or challenge publication found (eosinophilic oesophagitis only); GSK679586: no model beyond the draft's tracks (Hodsman 2013, De Boever 2014).
Baverel 2015 tralokinumab adolescent PK (PMID 26182954): a PK bridging analysis with no prediction compared with an outcome.
Grunig 1998 IL-13 blockade OVA mouse (Science companion to Wills-Karp): the same wild-type OVA mouse system as the draft's ova-mouse-il13 track, not a new system.
Human IL-13 air-pouch mouse (FDA 761180, CAT354Rp037): an in-vivo PD assay with no patient counterpart readout and no comparison found.
Regulator reliance: none; no asthma approval or label expansion for any member rests on model data.
